html:
Antonín Dvořák was a composer, born in 1841 in Nelahozeves near Prague, the son of a butcher and innkeeper, whose music drew on Czech and Slavic folk dances and won world fame.

He played viola in a Prague orchestra for years before Johannes Brahms helped him publish his Slavonic Dances in 1878, which made his name. He wrote nine symphonies, concertos, chamber music and operas, including Rusalka. From 1892 to 1895 he led the National Conservatory in New York, where he wrote the Symphony From the New World, inspired by American landscapes and by African American and Native American music, which he urged Americans to use. He returned to Prague, where he died in 1904. With Bedřich Smetana he founded Czech national music, part of the revival that led to Czechoslovakia.
sum: Antonín Dvořák was a composer, born in 1841 in Nelahozeves near Prague, the son of a butcher and innkeeper, whose music drew on Czech and Slavic folk dances and won world fame.
